questions.q: How is the Drill-Down page's design philosophy different from the Executive Summary page's?
options: It uses the exact same visuals and slicers as the Executive Summary page
It's built for exploration and slicing, not a ten-second glance
It has no filters at all
It only shows data for one territory, hard-coded
questions.explain: The Operations Manager needs to explore by region and product line, which calls for a matrix and independent slicers, not fixed KPI cards alone.

questions.q: What does the Matrix visual on this page use for rows and columns?
options: Fact[SalesOrderID] on both rows and columns
TerritoryDim[TerritoryName] on rows, ProductDim[SubcategoryName] on columns
Date[Year] on rows, Date[WeekNumber] on columns
There is no Matrix visual on this page
questions.explain: The matrix lets the Operations Manager scan Total Sales across every territory/subcategory combination at once.

questions.q: Which fulfillment metric appears on this page but has no place on the Executive Summary page?
options: Pct of Company Total
Prior Week Sales
Total Sales (All Regions)
Avg Days to Ship
questions.explain: Avg Days to Ship is a delivery-timing metric that matters directly to Operations, unlike the executive-level benchmark measures.

questions.q: Why does this page use the plain [Total Sales] measure instead of [Total Sales (All Regions)]?
options: Every number on this page is supposed to respond to whichever region/subcategory is selected, with no filter override
Total Sales (All Regions) doesn't exist in this model
It doesn't matter which one is used here
The plain measure is faster to calculate
questions.explain: Unlike the executive page's benchmark card, nothing on this page needs filters stripped away — it should always reflect the current selection.

questions.q: What should be true about [Total Sales] on this page versus the Executive Summary page, for the same region selected on both?
options: They are unrelated numbers that have no reason to match
The Drill-Down page's number should always be larger
They should always differ by exactly 10%
They should agree, since they're the same underlying measure and filter logic
questions.explain: Both pages ultimately draw on the same real data and the same measure logic, so a mismatch for the same filter is a signal worth investigating.
